name: Network
blurb: One VPC per persistent environment: three subnet tiers, six interface endpoints, and the two paths that actually reach the public internet.
audience: Platform engineers, and network or security review
note: Ephemeral PR and personal stages build no network of their own. They import the development environment's nine subnet IDs, both security groups and the API Gateway endpoint ID through addExternalExports, so everything drawn inside the VPC is shared with development.

d.role: Everything CloudFront needs has to live here.
facts: A CloudWatch alarm can only notify a topic in its own region, and CloudFront's metrics are here — which is why the alarm relay topics and their KMS key (alias/{stage}-flex-alerts-relay-key) are created in this stack rather than in eu-west-2.

d.role: Every FLEX compute and network resource except the edge.
facts: Both REST APIs are AWS-managed endpoints outside the VPC; a Lambda only gets a network interface in it when its construct passes vpc and vpcSubnets.

d.role: Nine subnets, three per tier, one per pinned availability zone.
facts: Availability zones are pinned to eu-west-2a/b/c rather than looked up, so subnet CIDRs stay stable across deploys.
Flow logs are enabled on the VPC itself, so all three tiers are captured without any per-subnet configuration.
The VPC belongs to FlexCoreStack, which is only created for a persistent environment.

d.role: Carries the NAT gateways. No workload is ever placed here.
facts: Default route to the internet gateway — the only route table in the VPC that has one.

d.role: Home of every access: private function, and of the endpoint network interfaces.
facts: The PrivateEgress security group is created with allowAllOutbound: true, so no explicit egress rule is written for anything in this tier.
The six interface endpoints put their ENIs in these subnets: CDK's default subnet selection is PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS, so the isolated tier reaches them across the VPC CIDR.
Default route goes to the NAT gateway in the same availability zone.

d.role: The default tier: every domain except dvla, plus the UDP and UNS gateways.
facts: The PrivateIsolated security group sets allowAllOutbound: false; the only rules it ever gets are 443 to each endpoint's security group, generated one per endpoint.
Its NACL has no ephemeral-return rule and no allow-all outbound rule — outbound is allowed only to the VPC CIDR (rule 80).
Its route tables carry only the local route: no NAT, no internet gateway.

d.tech: Other AWS accounts in the same organisation
d.role: Sibling systems, reached privately rather than over the internet.
Resolves the service name to the distribution.
facts: The hosted zone id and name are imported from /infra/dns/* — the zone belongs to the platform team, not to FLEX.
Persistent environments use the zone apex; every other stage gets {stage}.{zone}.

d.role: TLS identity for the distribution.
facts: Must be issued in us-east-1 — CloudFront will not accept a certificate from any other region.
Issued for whichever name applies to the stage and validated against the same hosted zone.

d.role: The single public entry point for the API.
facts: #createCloudfrontShield early-exits when the environment is development, so development and every ephemeral stage run with no Shield protection and no DDoS alarms.
publishAdditionalMetrics: true is what makes the error-rate alarm possible.
Access logs go to an object-locked bucket with 90-day GOVERNANCE retention.

d.role: The origin behind the /docs* behaviour.
facts: Retained in persistent environments; created with autoDeleteObjects and destroyed with every ephemeral stage.

d.role: The public surface, fronted by the regional WAF.
facts: The regional Web ACL blocks by default and allows only requests carrying the x-origin-verify secret header, so the origin cannot usefully be reached except through CloudFront.
SecurityPolicy_TLS13_1_2_2021_06 is set on the API itself, on top of the edge's TLS 1.2 minimum.

d.role: AWS-managed, not a resource inside the VPC — the interface endpoint is the door into it.
facts: Its resource policy denies execute-api:Invoke for any principal whose aws:SourceVpce is not this endpoint, and adds no explicit Allow.
Execution logging is INFO with dataTraceEnabled: false; only this API has it.

d.role: Stands in for the Cognito JWKS endpoint in the development environment.
facts: Created only when the environment is development, and with no vpc or vpcSubnets — it runs outside the VPC entirely.
Its unauthenticated Function URL is handed to the authorizer as JWKS_URI, so the authorizer reaches it over NAT and the public internet like any other external host.
It reads one hard-coded secret, /development/flex-secret/auth/e2e/private_jwk, cached for 300 seconds.

nodes.label: NAT gateways × 3
nodes.sub: one per AZ · one Elastic IP each

d.role: The only way out of the VPC to the internet.
facts: natGateways: 3 — one per availability zone, so losing an AZ does not remove egress for the other two.
The three Elastic IPs are the source addresses a third party such as DVLA sees.

d.role: Verifies the Cognito access token in front of every public route.
facts: It is in this tier because it fetches the JWKS over the public internet: there is no cognito-idp interface endpoint.
The verifier is constructed inside the handler, not at module scope, so JWKS_URI is re-read and re-parsed on every invocation.

d.role: The only workload that dials a non-AWS host.
facts: access: "private" in its gateway config is the whole reason it sits here; the UDP and UNS gateways declare isolated and land in the other tier.

d.role: The only domain whose route functions are in the egress tier.
facts: common.access: "private" in domain.config.ts moves all eight here; every other domain leaves the default and lands in the isolated tier.
They never use the internet route it buys them — every handler reaches DVLA through the DVLA gateway on the private API.

d.role: Reach their upstreams through the API Gateway interface endpoint.
facts: No NAT and no internet-gateway route, so whatever host they dial has to resolve to something reachable from inside the VPC.

UNS's consumer config declares a privateApiUrl and the gateway uses it as its base URL. UDP's schema has no such field at all — its gateway dials consumerConfig.apiUrl, which is not in this repo, so reachability depends on that URL resolving through the endpoint.

d.role: The default placement: a route function lands here unless its domain sets access.
facts: 29 route functions in development against 12 in production — the difference is which domains list which environments, not any network setting.
A route declared access: "public" would get no VPC configuration at all, but nothing in the repo declares one.

nodes.label: Interface endpoints × 6
nodes.sub: API GW · Logs · Secrets · SSM · STS

d.role: The isolated tier's only way to reach anything.
facts: Every endpoint security group is opened to the VPC CIDR on 443 by CDK (open defaults to true); the KMS endpoint additionally gets one explicit ingress rule per isolated subnet CIDR.
There is no cognito-idp endpoint and no X-Ray endpoint — the authorizer's JWKS fetch goes over NAT, and X-Ray segments are emitted by the Lambda execution environment rather than through the VPC.

Secrets Manager and SSM are here because secret and ssm:runtime resources resolve at runtime; ssm resources are already resolved to their value at deploy time and kms contributes only a key ARN, with decrypt called at runtime through the KMS endpoint.
The API Gateway endpoint's ID is exported as /{env}/flex/vpc-e/api-gateway and pinned into the private API's aws:SourceVpce condition. No gateway endpoints (S3, DynamoDB) exist.

d.role: Full-fidelity records of every flow in the VPC, delivered by AWS rather than by any subnet.
facts: Extended past ALL_DEFAULT_FIELDS with VPC ID, subnet ID, instance ID, TCP flags, packet source and destination addresses and flow direction.
The only statement the stack adds is the write path for delivery.logs.amazonaws.com; CDK's default account-root statement is also present.

No reader grant is written on top of CDK's default account-root kms:* statement, so decrypt is delegated to IAM rather than blocked outright — an investigator or Athena role still has to be granted it deliberately.
The bucket is object-locked at 365 days GOVERNANCE with a matching expiry rule.

d.role: Reached through NAT by the DVLA gateway and by the authorizer Lambda (Cognito JWKS, or the stub JWKS Function URL in development).
facts: The only internet egress out of the VPC. Non-VPC Lambdas (smoke test, dev JWKS stub) reach the internet via the Lambda service network instead.

d.tech: AWS APIs · SigV4 as an assumed role
d.role: Reached from the isolated tier through the API Gateway endpoint, never over the internet.
facts: Sibling systems in other GOV.UK Once accounts — inside the organisational boundary, outside this account.

d.carries: Swagger UI and the generated specs
facts: The only behaviour with caching enabled (CACHING_OPTIMIZED) and the only one that redirects HTTP to HTTPS rather than refusing it.
Caching is disabled on this behaviour, so every request crosses the region boundary to the origin.
originPath is /prod — the public API's only stage.
API Gateway invokes the function through the Lambda service, so nothing about this hop touches the VPC — only the function's own outbound calls do.
A second internet egress path alongside the DVLA gateway's, and the reason the authorizer cannot be an isolated function.

d.auth: API key plus a DVLA-issued bearer token

d.carries: The only internet egress out of the VPC

d.auth: None — the Function URL is unauthenticated
facts: The authorizer's JWKS_URI points at this public Function URL in development, so the request leaves through NAT and comes back in through the Lambda service.

d.auth: SigV4 with the function's own role
d.carries: Private API calls to the DVLA gateway and the udp domain
Private API calls plus Secrets Manager, SSM, STS and KMS
facts: The isolated security group has no other egress rule, so nothing beyond these six endpoints is reachable.

d.auth: sts:AssumeRole through the STS endpoint, then SigV4
Endpoint condition plus the caller's IAM policy
SigV4 as the assumed consumer role

tables.name: Address plan
rows: Via the NAT gateway in the same AZ
access: private — authorizer, DVLA gateway, all 8 dvla domain routes, and the six endpoint ENIs
access: isolated — UDP and UNS gateways plus every other domain's routes

tables.name: Network ACLs · subnet-level, stateless, first match wins in ascending rule order
rows: Rule 80 is the only pair that matches, so traffic may leave to the VPC CIDR and nowhere else

tables.name: Security groups · instance-level, stateful
rows: None — all outbound is already permitted
Authorizer, DVLA gateway, every access: private domain route
Egress TCP 443 to each of the six endpoint security groups, generated one per addVpcEndpoint call
UDP and UNS gateways, every access: isolated domain route
Every endpoint SG allows 443 from the VPC CIDR (CDK default); the KMS endpoint additionally gets an explicit rule per isolated subnet CIDR
One per interface endpoint, created by CDK

tables.name: VPC interface endpoints
rows: Reaching the private REST API — and, for the isolated gateways, the partner private APIs. Its endpoint ID is the pin in the private API's resource policy
Environment-variable decryption and consumer CMK operations — the one endpoint also reached by subnet CIDR, not only by security group
cognito-idp (the authorizer goes over NAT instead), X-Ray (segments leave through the execution environment), and any gateway endpoint for S3 or DynamoDB

tables.name: Egress paths
rows: Egress subnet → NAT gateway → internet gateway
DVLA APIs on the public internet
One of two internet egress paths — the authorizer also reaches out over NAT to fetch the Cognito JWKS (a public Lambda Function URL in development)
Egress subnet → NAT gateway → internet gateway
cognito-idp.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com, or the stub Function URL in development
There is no cognito-idp interface endpoint, so this cannot be an isolated function
Isolated subnet → API Gateway interface endpoint
No NAT, no internet route. UNS's config names a privateApiUrl; UDP's schema has no such field, so its apiUrl has to resolve through the endpoint
Secrets Manager, SSM, STS, KMS, CloudWatch Logs
443 only — enforced by SG rules for the isolated tier; the egress tier permits all outbound and simply happens to use 443
Other domains and the service gateways
SigV4 signed with the function's own role, and single-attempt — nothing on this path opts into retries
No third-party credentials are configured anywhere; isolated routes additionally have no network path — private-access routes such as the whole dvla domain do have one
The smoke test and the development JWKS stub bypass the VPC entirely

tables.name: Public ingress and TLS
rows: New TLS session to the origin
HSTS 365 days with includeSubdomains, on both behaviours
An app-wide aspect denies s3:* when aws:SecureTransport is false
